newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African industrial shares took a blow in mixed trading on Friday with dealers saying the index had been a victim of a sagging Dow Jones overnight, profit-taking and some poor economic data.
They said the industrial index also suffered from nervousness that world markets might slump after bearish comments by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan on Wednesday.
Greenspan warned that U.S. stock prices may have risen to too far and hinted that the Federal Reserve could hike U.S. interest rates.
South Africa's industrial index dropped 79.4 points to 8,244.3, the gold index ended down 22.6 points to 1,565.5 and the overall index lost 50.7 points to 7,145.3.
"The market has been pretty weak. Golds are down and industrials are also down," one dealer said.

"The main reasons are that we've got a weaker Dow, we had Greenspan's comments and the credit extension and money supply figures on paper today (Friday). So all these factors are all negative for our industrials," he dealer added.
Golds were soft for most of the day with dealers saying many market players did not believe the recent bullish trend in the bullion price could hold on for longer.
The yellow metal price shot through the psychologically important $360 per ounce level early on Friday, but by about 1447 GMT it had fallen back by about a dollar.
"I think many people are waiting to see if the price can hold at this level because too many people have been hit too often at this one," another dealer said.

Dealers put Friday's volumes between 800 and 900 million rand, adding some futures activity had also hit the industrials. They said the market now awaited Finance Minister Trevor Manuels's March 12 budget speech for some direction.

"I think the market is still going to be a little bit negative...probably we'll see the market being weaker at the end of next week from negative sentiment, (but) I hope the budget that's coming up is going to be good for the market," one dealer said.
The dealers said some of the market players had shown keen interest in the Gencor stock which shed 15 cents to halt at 19.40 rand and Trencor which added 40 cents to 22.20 rand.
Sasol shed 140 cents to 48.50 rand and RMB Holdings dropped 100 cents to 96.00 rand.
Near-dated gold shares ended softer on the back of better bullion price -- but shrouded in uncertainty, and the industrial contract weak on a poor Dow Jones on Thursday.
The March all-share contract was down at 6,485/500 from 6,578, the industrial contrcat slipped to 7,927/40 from 8,060 and the gold contract edged down at 1,100/08 from 1,125.
